It uses only the\nRuby standard library plus SQLite, keeps all domain logic in named modules,\nand implements a tiny TCP/HTTP layer at the bottom of the file.\n\n## Quick start\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` is a one-line wrapper that executes `ruby server.rb`. The server\nbinds to `127.0.0.1` and reads the port from the `PORT` environment variable\n(defaulting to `3000`).\n\nVerify it is listening:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# => {\"ok\":true}\n```\n\nThe server runs in the foreground; stop it with `Ctrl-C` or by sending\n`SIGTERM` to the process.\n\n## Entry point and file layout\n\n- `run.sh` — the launcher required by the harness.\n- `server.rb` — the only source file. It is organized from top to bottom as:\n  1. `Config` — constants (host, port, DB path, schema version).\n  2. `PureRules` — deterministic, side-effect-free game-rule helpers.\n  3. `Persistence` — SQLite schema, connection wrapper, and lifecycle helpers.\n  4. `Combat` — combat sessions, initiative, and turn/condition tracking.\n  5. `Compendium` — monster and item reference entries.\n  6. `Campaigns` — campaign metadata, characters, and event logs.\n  7. `Factions` — campaign factions, NPCs, and relationship summaries.\n  8. `Inventory` — campaign inventory and character equipment assignments.\n  9. `Crafting` — downtime crafting projects and progress.\n  10. `Auth` — PBKDF2 password hashing and user storage.\n  11. `PlayerHandbook` — PHB rule helpers (spell slots, rests, encumbrance).\n  12. `DmTools` — DM-facing helpers (encounter builder, loot, session recap).\n  13. `Sessions` — campaign session scheduling and attendance.\n  14. `Request` / `Response` / `Router` / `HttpServer` — transport layer.\n\nThe bottom of the file calls `HttpServer.run` when the file is executed\ndirectly.\n\n## State, persistence, and routing\n\n### Persistence design\n\n- SQLite file: `game.db` in the working directory.\n- A single `Mutex` (`Persistence::DB_MUTEX`) serializes all database access.\n- `Persistence.db` yields a single shared `SQLite3::Database` connection that\n  is opened when the module loads and reused for the lifetime of the process.\n  This keeps the implementation simple and deterministic.\n- On startup the server calls `Persistence.initialize_schema!`. The schema\n  statements use `IF NOT EXISTS`, so existing data is preserved across restarts\n  and new tables are created automatically.\n- `Persistence.reset!` drops every application table and recreates the schema.\n  It is used by the `/v1/storage/reset` endpoint.\n\n### Request routing\n\n- Raw socket I/O: `TCPServer` accepts connections; each connection is handled\n  in its own thread so the accept loop is never blocked. `Request.parse`\n  reads a request line, headers, and optional body.\n- `Router.route` is a long `if/elsif` dispatch that matches `method + path`.\n  Path parameters are captured with anchored regexes and forced to UTF-8 so\n  SQLite binds them as text rather than blobs.\n- Connections are kept open until the client closes them, supporting HTTP/1.1\n  keep-alive without pipelining issues.\n- Domain modules return `[:tag, data]` tuples:\n  - `:ok` with a Hash body,\n  - `:invalid` for validation failures,\n  - `:not_found` for missing resources,\n  - `:conflict` for duplicate IDs.\n- `Router.handle_result` maps those tags to HTTP status codes (`200`, `201`,\n  `400`, `404`, `409`) and serializes the body as JSON.\n- Authentication endpoints (`/v1/auth/*`) are handled specially in the router\n  because `Auth` returns booleans rather than tuples. A successful login\n  returns a deterministic `session-<username>` token.\n\n## Main API/domain groupings\n\n| Group | Endpoints | Module |\n|-------|-----------|--------|\n| Core | `/health`, `/v1/dice/stats`, `/v1/checks/ability`, `/v1/encounters/adjusted-xp`, `/v1/initiative/order` | `PureRules` |\n| Characters | `/v1/characters/ability-modifier`, `/v1/characters/proficiency`, `/v1/characters/derived-stats` | `PureRules` |\n| Combat | `/v1/combat/sessions`, `/v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`, `/v1/combat/sessions/:id/advance` | `Combat` |\n| Auth | `/v1/auth/register`, `/v1/auth/login` | `Auth` |\n| Storage | `/v1/storage/status`, `/v1/storage/reset` | `Persistence` |\n| Compendium | `/v1/compendium/monsters`, `/v1/compendium/monsters/:slug`, `/v1/compendium/items`, `/v1/compendium/items/:slug` | `Compendium` |\n| Campaigns | `/v1/campaigns`, `/v1/campaigns/:id/characters`, `/v1/campaigns/:id/events`, `/v1/campaigns/:id/state` | `Campaigns` |\n| Factions | `/v1/campaigns/:id/factions`, `/v1/campaigns/:id/npcs`, `/v1/campaigns/:id/relationships` | `Factions` |\n| Inventory | `/v1/campaigns/:id/inventory`, `/v1/campaigns/:id/characters/:character_id/equipment`, `/v1/campaigns/:id/inventory/summary` | `Inventory` |\n| Session scheduling | `/v1/campaigns/:id/sessions`, `/v1/campaigns/:id/sessions/:session_id/attendance`, `/v1/campaigns/:id/sessions/next` | `Sessions` |\n| PHB rules | `/v1/phb/spell-slots`, `/v1/phb/rests/long`, `/v1/phb/equipment-load` | `PlayerHandbook` |\n| DM tools | `/v1/dm/encounter-builder`, `/v1/dm/loot-parcel`, `/v1/dm/session-recap` | `DmTools` |\n\n## Conventions for extending and testing\n\n### Adding a new endpoint\n\n1. If the endpoint is pure computation, put it in the appropriate domain\n   module (e.g., `PureRules`, `PlayerHandbook`, `DmTools`) and have it return\n   a Hash on success or `nil` on invalid input.\n2. If the endpoint needs persistence, add it to the module that owns the data\n   (e.g., `Combat`, `Campaigns`, `Compendium`) and return a `[:tag, data]`\n   tuple.\n3. Wire the endpoint into `Router.route` with an explicit `method`/`path` check\n   and call `handle_result` or `json_response` / `error_response` as needed.\n4. If the endpoint creates a resource, use status `201`; otherwise use `200`.\n\n### Adding a new table\n\n1. Add the `CREATE TABLE` statement to `Persistence::SCHEMA_SQL`.\n2. Add the table name to the drop list in `Persistence.reset!`.\n3. Add a module that owns reads and writes for that table.\n4. Keep validation logic private with `private_class_method`.\n\n### Testing locally\n\nBecause the server is a single file, you can run it directly:\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ruby server.rb\n```\n\nThen exercise endpoints with `curl` or any HTTP client. To reset state between\nmanual test runs, use:\n\n```bash\ncurl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/v1/storage/reset\n```\n\nFor automated regression testing, run the `dndeval` suite against the running\nserver. The cumulative `dm-tools` suite exercises every endpoint above and\nverifies the prior-stage behavior.\n\n### Determinism\n\n- Game-rule helpers are pure functions of their inputs.\n- Combat initiative uses deterministic tie-breaking (`score`, then `dex`, then\n  name).\n- `DmTools.loot_parcel` is deterministic for a given tier and seed; it does\n  not use `SecureRandom`.\n- Password hashing still uses `SecureRandom` for salts, which is correct for\n  security and does not affect the deterministic test flows that register and\n  then immediately authenticate the same user.\n\n### What to avoid\n\n- Do not introduce Rack, Rails, Sinatra, or external gems.
